summary.headline: Ambuja Cements Q2 FY27 consol EBITDA INR1,271 crore (~14% margin, INR770/t) on 16.5 Mt volume; 14 expansion projects add ~30 Mt grinding, capex INR14,500 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 cement volume was 16.5 Mt, revenue INR9,197 crore, EBITDA INR1,271 crore (about 14% margin, INR770/t) and PAT INR236 crore, with the company still debt-free. Trade volumes rose 8.6% YoY and trade share reached 74%, while non-trade (B2B) volumes remained negative, leaving total volume roughly flat. Management announced a 14-project expansion (about 30 Mt grinding, 10.3 Mt clinker) costing about INR14,500 crore, taking capacity to 149 Mt by FY29 and 155 Mt by FY30. Unit cost fell to INR4,410/t (INR4,182/t normalised), with FY27 target of INR4,250/t reiterated.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 fuel cost INR1.66/kcal; Q2 FY26 INR1.60/kcal
vs INR6/unit in Q2 FY26 and INR4.3/unit in Q1 FY27

segments.name: Trade (consol)
segments.commentary: Trade volumes up 8.6% YoY; trade share up to 74%; premium products 37% of trade sales (35% last year). West trade volume +14%, North +13%, South +13%, Central +9%, East flat.

segments.name: Non-trade / institutional (B2B)
segments.commentary: Deliberately recalibrated to drop negative-EBITDA volumes; still negative YoY in Q2, with management expecting positive growth in Q3 and Q4. Blended cement share 82% of sales vs 77% a year ago.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete (RMC)
segments.commentary: Quarterly volume 1.07 million cubic metres, up 19% YoY, from a network of about 125 plants; RMC EBITDA margin about 7% per management.

segments.name: Green power / fly ash
segments.commentary: Green power sales about INR136 crore (352 million kWh) in Q2, booked in other operating income; fly ash revenue about INR25 crore. Combined contribution about INR97/t per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cost target of INR4,250/t reiterated; management says ~INR160/t improvement is needed in H2 and that it is on track, subject to no further global fuel escalation.
H2 FY27 volume growth guided to be ahead of industry, at higher single digit (aim for double digit) against industry growth of about 6-7% for FY27.
Capacity to reach 149 Mt by FY29 and 155 Mt by FY30; FY28 cost target of INR4,000/t for combined existing and new capacity.
Capex: about INR14,500 crore for the 30 Mt programme (~INR7,500 crore a year over the next two years). FY27 capex guided at INR6,500-7,000 crore, with INR3,000-3,500 crore in H2.
Merger of ACC and Orient Cement into Ambuja to go to NCLT; completion expected within FY27 and described as EPS accretive.
Realisation: INR10/bag price increase realised in October; further hikes expected. Management sees about INR150/t benefit from trade mix by June 2027.
capex_capacity: Q2 commissioned 4.6 Mt at Dahej (Gujarat), Salai Banwa (UP) and Kalamboli (Maharashtra); 3.2 Mt at Bathinda (Punjab) and Penna Jodhpur (Rajasthan) stabilised with ramp-up in H2; 2.4 Mt at Warisaliganj (Bihar) due Q3 FY27.
Expansion: 30 Mt grinding (West 15.2 Mt, East 11.6 Mt, North 2.9 Mt) and 10.3 Mt clinker (Maratha 4 Mt, Umrangso 4 Mt, Mundra 2.25 Mt).
Execution timelines of about 14 months for grinding units and about 18 months for integrated units; equipment reportedly already ordered and PMC appointed. Around 20 Mt bunched into March-May 2028.
Penna and Sanghi utilisation about 50% in Q2; company-level utilisation about 61-62% in Q2, targeted at about 75% by end FY27.
Clinker capacity 69 Mt with clinker factor about 66%. Debottlenecking at about four plants with Loesche expected to complete in 4-5 months.
demand_pricing: Price held at INR255/bag in the monsoon-hit Q2; INR10/bag realised in October with more hikes expected.
Management says the trade-led push adds about INR40/t so far, rising toward INR150/t by June 2027.
Demand headwinds: weak monsoon with drought declared in several large states (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra, Rajasthan); impact expected with a lag in Q3-Q4.
Brand equity claimed to support a price premium, backed by independent surveys. Competition in East and West expansion regions acknowledged; management says 'there is a market for everyone'.
Fuel: blended fuel cost INR1.87/kcal in Q2 vs spot imported coal INR2.80-2.85/kcal; domestic coal above 60% of mix, imported under 40% (pet coke about 10-12%).

qa_highlights.question: Why revisit expansion now when H1 volumes were negative and demand soft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly performance did not drive the decision; the first capex wave is nearly complete and the second wave (West, East, North) is value-accretive, mostly brownfield and clinker-backed. Earlier guidance of 140 Mt by FY28 and 155 Mt by FY30 is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Total capex needed to reach 149 Mt, and how will debt evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR14,500 crore for 30 Mt, roughly INR7,500 crore a year. Management described the programme as self-sustainable from cash flows, with only interim debt possible.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cost guidance of INR4,000/t: does it include new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR4,000/t target for FY28 covers the combined existing and new capacity at 149 Mt.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in execution given past delays and bunched-up commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lessons from the first phase, including a contractor issue, and a tighter scheduling plan with 14-18 month build cycles. It did not name specific suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: Expected H2 volume growth and Q3 cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 volume growth is guided to higher single digit, aiming for double digit, ahead of industry. The cost path is supported by green power, BCFC, WHRS (18 MW at Sanghi in Q3) and AFR.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate low in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to the proposed merger and the tax shield from Penna and Sanghi, which it said is one driver of EPS accretion.

risks_watch: Execution risk: about 20 Mt of capacity bunched in March-May 2028 on 14-18 month build cycles, with prior contractor issues.
Cost risk: fuel costs rising (spot imported coal INR2.80-2.85/kcal vs blend INR1.87); FY27 target depends on INR160/t H2 improvement and no further escalation.
Demand risk: drought in major states may moderate construction with a lag; non-trade volumes still negative.
Utilisation of acquired Penna and Sanghi assets at about 50% in Q2; management withheld detailed figures until Q3-Q4.
Merger completion via NCLT and EPS accretion claims; Q2 tax rate unusually low on merger-linked tax shield.
Management's previously stated 'aggressive' vs 'calibrated' expansion framing was questioned by analysts and left unresolved.
summary.management_tone: Confident on cost, trade growth and the expansion roadmap, but defensive when pressed on why capex is accelerating after weak H1 volumes. Management was evasive on specific numbers (Assam capex, Penna/Sanghi utilisation, spot fuel) and deferred several details to later updates.
key_quotes: So this is nothing as per any sense of change. We are now following our defined pathway, which we had guided before.
Closer to INR14,500 crores will be what we require for this 30 million tons, which has a combination of IUs and GUs.
As a going -- running company, we are giving INR4,000 combination of existing and new.
So we had a program of INR6,500 crores to INR7,000 crores for this year.
